content.user_title: Build B2B EVP Briefs Across Buyer Awareness Tiers
content.value_statement: B2B messaging loses relevance when it assumes every buyer has the same awareness. This skill organizes value propositions, proof, and placements into three audience-specific tiers.
actual_capabilities: Confirm one ideal customer profile segment before creating the brief.
Capture pain context, desired outcomes, tradeoffs, optional competitors, and optional proof.
Describe audience knowledge and pain framing for problem-aware, solution-aware, and product-aware buyers.
Draft one primary and one alternate EVP per tier using 22-word line placeholders.
Align proof to pain, category comparisons, and specific competitor differences.
Recommend deployment surfaces, including landing pages, ads, cold email, pricing pages, and sales materials.
limitations: Covers awareness Tiers 2, 3, and 4 only, with one customer segment per brief.
Depends on supplied evidence and does not independently verify metrics or competitor claims.
Marked as a non-user-invocable sub-skill loaded by the parent evp skill.
References a separate framework document that is not included in the reviewed single-file package.

use_cases.title: Align Campaign Messaging
use_cases.description: Create tier-specific messaging and proof recommendations for landing pages, advertisements, and email campaigns.

use_cases.title: Clarify Competitive Positioning
use_cases.description: Organize category comparisons and vendor differences into one brief for a selected customer segment.

use_cases.title: Prepare Sales Messaging
use_cases.description: Translate audience awareness into sales openers, objection responses, and battlecard messaging.

prompt_templates.title: Create a First Brief
prompt_templates.prompt: Build an EVP brief for [customer segment]. Our customers struggle with [pain]. We deliver [outcome] without [tradeoff]. Ask for any missing inputs.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: establish one audience and the essential messaging inputs.

prompt_templates.title: Use Existing Pain Research
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a three-tier EVP brief for [segment] using this PSP document: [document]. Include primary and alternate lines, proof needs, and deployment surfaces.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: turn an existing pain document into structured messaging.

prompt_templates.title: Add Competitive Context
prompt_templates.prompt: Build the brief for [segment] with [outcome], [tradeoff], and competitors [names]. Use only these verified differences: [evidence]. Label missing proof explicitly.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: connect category and vendor positioning to supplied evidence.

prompt_templates.title: Refresh an Existing Brief
prompt_templates.prompt: Refresh this brief for [segment]: [brief]. Incorporate these market changes and verified proof: [updates]. Revise all three tiers, variants, and placement recommendations.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: update messaging during a periodic positioning review.

output_examples.input: Build a brief for finance leads at growing SaaS companies. Our tool automates invoice reconciliation without replacing accounting software. No proof supplied.
output: PSP anchor: Finance leads lose time reconciling invoices manually.

Tier 2: Problem-aware buyers need pain framing. Primary EVP: Stop losing finance hours to manual invoice reconciliation and give your growing SaaS team clearer numbers without replacing the accounting software today.
Alternate: Give finance teams time back by automating invoice reconciliation across SaaS operations without forcing an accounting software migration or adding manual steps.
Proof needed: Document reconciliation time and error frequency. Deploy on landing pages and early-stage ads.
Tier 3: Compare automation with manual reconciliation. Proof needed: A measured workflow comparison. Deploy on comparison pages and sales openers.
Tier 4: Competitor context is missing. Request verified vendor differences before drafting comparison claims. Deploy verified messaging on pricing pages and battlecards.

output_examples.input: Show the deployment recommendations for a completed three-tier brief aimed at operations managers.
output: Problem-aware: Use pain-focused messaging on landing pages, early-stage ads, and cold emails tied to relevant awareness signals.
Solution-aware: Use category comparisons on comparison pages, mid-funnel ads, and sales openers for prospects who have tried alternatives.
Product-aware: Use verified vendor differences on pricing pages, battlecards, objection responses, and bottom-funnel ads.
Review the brief every 90 days as market conditions and competitor positioning change.

best_practices: Create a separate brief for each customer segment and describe its pain in customer language.
Supply verified metrics and competitor evidence, and label unsupported proof as missing.
Match each placement to buyer awareness and review the brief every 90 days.
anti_patterns: Combining unrelated customer segments into one brief.
Presenting illustrative metrics or unsupported competitor claims as verified evidence.
Using product comparisons for buyers who have not yet recognized their problem.

faq.question: Which awareness levels does the brief cover?
faq.answer: It covers Tier 2, problem-aware; Tier 3, solution-aware; and Tier 4, product-aware.

faq.question: What inputs should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide one customer segment, pain context or a PSP document, the desired outcome, and the tradeoff avoided. Competitors and proof are optional.

faq.question: Can one brief cover multiple customer segments?
faq.answer: The workflow requires one segment per brief. Create a separate brief for each additional segment.

faq.question: Does it verify proof or research competitors?
faq.answer: No independent verification or competitor research workflow is specified. Supply reliable evidence and review comparison claims before publication.

faq.question: How is this sub-skill activated?
faq.answer: It is marked non-user-invocable and loaded by the parent evp skill when a full brief is requested.

faq.question: Does it publish the generated messaging?
faq.answer: No publishing workflow is specified. It produces a messaging brief with placement recommendations for later use.
